description: The login endpoint concatenates the username parameter directly into a SQL query, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and read the users table.

evidence.notes: Authenticated as user id 1 without a valid password.

impact: Full authentication bypass and disclosure of all user records, including password hashes.
proof_of_concept: POST /login username=' OR 1=1 -- password=x => HTTP 200 with session cookie for user id 1.
remediation: Use parameterized queries for all database access and enforce least-privilege database credentials.
steps_to_reproduce: Send a POST request to /login with username set to `' OR 1=1 --` and any password.
Observe that the response returns an authenticated session for the first user in the table.
Repeat with a UNION SELECT payload to exfiltrate rows from the users table.
title: SQL injection in login username parameter

description: Unhandled exceptions on the profile page return stack traces that disclose internal file paths and framework versions.
impact: An attacker learns internal paths and framework versions, aiding further attacks.
remediation: Return a generic error page and log the stack trace server-side only.
steps_to_reproduce: Request /profile with an invalid user id such as /profile?id=%%.
Observe the 500 response body contains a stack trace with internal paths.
title: Verbose error messages disclose internal paths

description: The robots.txt file lists an administrative path that is not linked from the site navigation.
impact: Minor information disclosure of a path an attacker can probe directly.
remediation: Remove sensitive paths from robots.txt or protect the path with authentication.
steps_to_reproduce: Request /robots.txt and note the Disallow entry for /admin/.
Request /admin/ and observe the login prompt.
title: robots.txt discloses administrative path
